newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta shares end lower on consolidation.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta shares end lower on consolidation.

text.p: Jakarta shares ended lower on Wednesday as the market remained in a consolidation phase with mainly speculative trading, brokers said.
The Jakarta Composite Index fell 1.56 points, or 0.26 percent, to close at 595.49 points after touching a low for the day of 591.90 points. Losers led gainers by 54 to 51, with 60 counters unchanged.
Brokers said the market was likely to continue consolidating on Thursday with the index staying within a narrow range.
Brokers expected trading to lack direction for the rest of the week, with significant movements in only a few counters.

"There is no direction to the market. I expect it will recover next week after refunds from Bank Negara Indonesia subscriptions. Then there could some fresh money entering the market," a foreign broker said.
Brokers said active locally-led speculative buying of some medium and small-sized stocks, including banking issues, had kept the index from falling further.
Seasoning producer Miwon Indonesia topped the active list with about eight million shares traded, rising 100 rupiah to 2,550 rupiah.
Bank BDNI and Bank International Indonesia were also active.
BDNI rose 50 rupiah to 2,000 on a volume of 3.7 million shares, while Bank International Indonesia rose 50 rupiah to 2,025 on 2.5 million shares.
Brokers said the banking sector had benefitted from the well-received BNI public offering last week.
Telecommunications cable producer Voksel also traded actively on what brokers said was market talk of a possible merger. Company officials were not available for comment.
It ended up 25 at 800 rupiah on a volume of 1.8 million shares after earlier touching 900 rupiah.
Brokers said blue chips Telkom, Citra Marga and Indosat were among the targets for foreign profit taking. Telkom fell 25 rupiah to 3,825 rupiah on a volume of 2.1 million shares.
Toll road operator Citra Marga fell 100 rupiah to 2,075 rupiah on a volume of 1.2 million shares.
